title: Long-range expanders: construction and cutoff
summary: Long-range expansion is a combinatorial graph property introduced to construct metric spaces with strong quantitative obstructions to low-distortion embeddings. Such extremal constructions are motivated by fundamental questions in metric geometry and nonlinear functional analysis. However, the only known constructions of long-range expander sequences are random regular graphs; the problem of constructing explicit sequences, especially with logarithmic girth, remains open.
